
```{r, child = "setup.Rmd", include = FALSE}
```

When a function builds one result from several inputs, the inputs must agree
on their names. If they don't, the function errors instead of silently picking
one input's names.

These functions follow the rules:

- [rray_add()], [rray_subtract()], [rray_multiply()], [rray_divide()], and
  [rray_exponentiate()]

- [rray_and()], [rray_or()], and [rray_xor()]

- [rray_pmax()] and [rray_pmin()]

- [rray_combine()] and [rray_stack()]

# Rules

For each axis of the result:

All inputs with names along that axis must have exactly the same names. If all
names are the same, the result has those names. If no input is named, the
result is not named. If any names are different, an error is thrown to avoid
arbitrarily picking between the inputs. If an input is broadcast or has no
names, it is excluded from common name determination.

To resolve a conflict, preemptively remove the names from one input with
[rray_set_names()].

# Examples

Matching names are kept, and different names are an error:

```{r, error = TRUE}
x <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2")))
y <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("a", "b")))

rray_add(x, x)

rray_add(x, y)

rray_add(x, rray_set_names(y, NULL))
```

An input without names on an axis has no say there. Here, each input names a
different axis, so both sets of names are kept:

```{r}
x <- array(1:4, c(2, 2), dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2"), NULL))
y <- array(5:8, c(2, 2), dimnames = list(NULL, c("c1", "c2")))

rray_add(x, y)
```

A broadcast axis has no say either. `"total"` names a single row that gets
repeated, so it no longer describes the result and is dropped:

```{r}
x <- array(1:3, c(1, 3), dimnames = list("total", c("a", "b", "c")))
y <- array(1:6, c(2, 3), dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2"), c("a", "b", "c")))

rray_multiply(x, y)
```

Empty names count, so `c("r1", "")` and `c("r1", "r2")` are different:

```{r, error = TRUE}
x <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "")))
y <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2")))

rray_add(x, y)
```

A named vector is a 1D array with names, so its names are checked too:

```{r, error = TRUE}
x <- array(1:4, c(2, 2), dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2"), c("c1", "c2")))

rray_multiply(x, c(a = 10, b = 20))

rray_multiply(x, c(10, 20))
```

# Combining and stacking

[rray_combine()] never checks names on `.axis`. They are pasted together from
every input, with `""` for inputs that have none. Every other axis follows the
rules above:

```{r, error = TRUE}
a <- array(1:2, c(1, 2), dimnames = list("r1", c("x", "y")))
b <- array(3:4, c(1, 2))
c <- array(5:6, c(1, 2), dimnames = list("r3", c("x", "z")))

rray_combine(a, b, c, .axis = 1)

c <- array(5:6, c(1, 2), dimnames = list("r3", c("x", "y")))

rray_combine(a, b, c, .axis = 1)
```

[rray_stack()] names the new axis with the names of `...`. Every other axis
follows the rules above, which catches data that was reordered:

```{r, error = TRUE}
jan <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("north", "south")))
feb <- array(3:4, 2, dimnames = list(c("south", "north")))

rray_stack(jan = jan, feb = feb, .axis = 2)
```

# Comparisons

Comparison functions like [rray_equal()] and [rray_greater_than()] return a
verdict about their inputs rather than a new value, so they return no names
and never check them:

```{r}
x <- array(c(TRUE, FALSE), 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2")))
y <- array(c(TRUE, TRUE), 2, dimnames = list(c("a", "b")))

rray_equal(x, y)
```
